subtopics.title: The Cost Table and the Three Cost Concepts

questions.question: Total cost at zero output is R20. What does this R20 represent?
options: Fixed cost — paid whether or not anything is produced
Marginal cost of the first unit

questions.question: Total cost is R60 at 3 units and R76 at 4 units. The marginal cost of the fourth unit is:
Average cost at 4 units (total cost R76) is:
Why does average cost FALL over the first few units of output?
options: Because the fixed cost is spread over more units
Because marginal cost is always rising

subtopics.title: Building the Revenue Side at a Market Price of R30

questions.question: At a market price of R30, total revenue at 5 units is:
For a price-taking firm, average revenue always equals:
Why is marginal revenue constant at R30 for this firm?
options: Because output never exceeds six units
Because each extra unit sells at the unchanged market price of R30

questions.question: Using total revenue minus total cost, profit at 5 units is:
The economist's rule for the profit-maximising output is to produce:
options: Until total cost equals total revenue
As many units as capacity allows
Until marginal revenue equals marginal cost, stopping before MC exceeds MR
Where average cost is at its minimum

questions.question: The sixth unit has marginal cost R38 against marginal revenue R30. Producing it would:
The firm still makes R40 profit at six units. Why is six NOT the right output?
options: Because profit at five units (R48) is higher — the sixth unit itself destroys profit
Because the firm cannot sell six units
Because fixed costs rise at six units

subtopics.title: Verifying, Graphing and the Habits That Earn Marks

questions.question: How do you verify the profit-maximising output 'from both sides'?
options: Compare total cost at zero and six units
Check the last produced unit adds profit (MC below MR) and the next unit would subtract profit (MC above MR)
Draw the demand curve for the industry

questions.question: On the graph, the profit-maximising output is found where:
options: The marginal cost curve crosses the flat marginal revenue line from below

questions.question: Which pair of verbs matches the two derived measures?
options: Average: divide; Marginal: subtract neighbouring totals

subtopics.title: Costs That Sleep and Costs That Work

questions.question: At the vetkoek stand, which of these is a cost that 'sleeps' — owed even on a day with no sales?
options: The table hire, gas bottle and licence for the spot
The cousin paid to help on a busy morning

questions.question: 'What did the LAST one cost me?' is answered by:
options: Subtracting this row's total cost from the row before it

questions.question: Total cost is R76 at 4 units and R102 at 5 units. What did the fifth unit cost on its own?
Why does the average cost per unit drop as the first few units are made?
options: Because the sleeping R20 is split between more and more units, so each carries a smaller slice

subtopics.title: Thirty Rand a Plate, Every Single Plate

questions.question: The stand cannot charge R40 or need to charge R20 — the market pays R30. This makes it:
Total revenue at 5 plates, at R30 a plate, is:
Why is average revenue R30 at every output level?
options: Because the stand sells exactly five plates
Because the money per plate can only be the price charged per plate
Because R30 is the average of all prices at the rank

questions.question: Pictured on a graph with plates along the bottom and rands up the side, marginal revenue for this stand is:
options: A curve shaped like a tick
A flat line lying level at the R30 mark

subtopics.title: Is the Next One Worth Making?

questions.question: Plate five brings in R30 and costs R26. The stand should:
options: Make it — it still adds R4
Refuse it — the cost is too close to the price

questions.question: Plate six brings in R30 and costs R38. Making it would:
options: Take R8 out of the stand's pocket

questions.question: At six plates the stand still earns R40 of profit. Why is six still the wrong answer?
options: Because six plates cannot be sold
Because fixed costs rise at six plates
Because five plates earn R48 — the right question is whether the NEXT one pays, not whether the day is profitable

questions.question: Described in words, the marginal cost line in this table:
options: Drops from R18 to R10 by the third plate, then swings sharply up through R16, R26 and R38 — a lopsided tick
Rises in equal steps of R30
